.53`... let's try `drill example.com @198.51.100.53` and `sysctl net.route`? Or check pf state counts for WAN traffic.

Let me try: pfctl -s states (was 127 for info/nat). Maybe states works. And unbound status.

Given time, I think enough evidence exists. Distinguish between:
- wan_dhcp_lease: stale lease / not renewed after modem re-registration
- modem: modem itself rebooted (already recovered per log)
- provider_network: cable signal issues (T3 timeout, TFTP config file NOT FOUND) — that was the initial cause at 02:01; then registration completed at 02:28, so provider path restored.

The current state: internet still down at 02:41 even though modem registered at 02:28 (13 min ago). The firewall hasn't refreshed its WAN configuration. That points to wan_dhcp_lease on gw.lan as the component: the running WAN config is stale relative to the modem's re-registration; a reload would renew it. Contributing: modem/provider event (T3 timeout + TFTP config failure) triggered the outage.

Hmm, but which is "the reason the internet is down"? If the modem re-registered and works, then the remaining break is on the firewall side: stale WAN lease → wan_reload fix. Alternatively, the fault could be provider_network still broken (registration complete but no data). We can't test external connectivity directly (ping 8.8.8.8 no recorded output). Ping to 198.51.100.1 (modem LAN IP) fails — that's the immediate next hop. If the modem were fully functional and forwarding, ping to its own interface address should typically reply (cable modems/CPE often do). But ICMP may be filtered.

Let me try a couple more probes: drill with @server, host command, netstat -rn already done. Also check unbound local resolver for whether DNS resolution works locally (local services work). Let's try `drill -v`? Not offered. Try `host example.com @198.51.100.53`.
Also `sockstat -4 -n -p 53` maybe.

Let me do two quick checks: host to provider resolver, and pfctl -s states.

data.reason: The ISP link dropped and the cable modem re-registered (new session at ~02:28), but the firewall's WAN interface still runs the pre-outage DHCP lease (198.51.100.27, renew not due until 2026/3/5), so its WAN addressing no longer matches what the provider side now serves and no traffic gets through; the watchdog only logged "would_reload" because it is in observe mode.

data.cause: The ISP link dropped and the cable modem re-registered (new session at ~02:28), but the firewall's WAN interface still runs the pre-outage DHCP lease (198.51.100.27, renew not due until 2026/3/5), so its WAN addressing no longer matches what the provider side now serves and no traffic gets through; the watchdog only logged "would_reload" because it is in observe mode.
evidence: cat /var/db/dhclient.leases.vtnet0: single stored lease, fixed-address 198.51.100.27, dhcp-server-identifier 203.0.113.67, renew 4 2026/3/5 09:12:40, expire 2026/3/6 - far in the future, so nothing would have renewed it during this outage.

tail /var/db/wan-watchdog/events.jsonl: outage_start 02:06 with cm_status NOT_SYNCHRONIZED; 02:29 decision "none, modem_settling" once cm_status became OPERATIONAL; 02:30 decision "reload, modem_operational" but logged as "would_reload ... mode: observe", and again 02:40 "would_reload, retry" - the reload was never applied.

cat /var/db/wan-watchdog/state.json: {"outage_start":1772521560,"reloads_in_outage":2,"last_reload":1772523600,"last_action":"reload","modem_op_since":1772522940} - modem operational since ~02:29 while the WAN is still down at 02:41.

tail/head /var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-metrics.jsonl and modem-events.jsonl: 02:01:44 "No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out", 02:14:10 "TFTP failed - configuration file NOT FOUND", 02:28:21 "Cable Modem Reboot ... registration complete"; metrics go NOT_SYNCHRONIZED (uptime 240) to OPERATIONAL with healthy plant stats (min_snr 37.9 dB), so the provider path itself has come back.
ifconfig vtnet0: UP,RUNNING,LOWER_UP, inet 198.51.100.27 - physical WAN link is up, so this is not a cable/link or NIC problem.

netstat -rn and arp -n: default route still via 198.51.100.1 with an ARP entry for it, yet ping -c 3 198.51.100.1 gives 100% packet loss - the stale on-link addressing explains why nothing passes even though the route and layer 2 look fine.
data.recommendation: Reconfigure the WAN interface on gw.lan (dhclient release/renew on vtnet0) so it takes a fresh address from the re-registered provider side; that is what the watchdog's own logic decided at 02:30 but could not do in observe mode. Afterwards, consider moving the watchdog out of observe mode so its modem_operational reload decision actually fires instead of only logging would_reload.
data.detail: stale WAN DHCP lease after modem re-registered
